fixed.what: The option analysis for three distractors did not reproduce their values (checked by enumerating every one- and two-line misclassification in python3). A said moving the 120m of loan repayments gives -200, but that gives 160 - 440 = -280; -200 comes from counting the 80m money-market borrowing (or the 80m deposit inflows) as a demand, 200 - 400. B said netting borrowing against repayment gives -80, but netting leaves the answer at -40; -80 comes from swapping the two borrowing lines, 260 - 340. D said reversing the subtraction (or importing the Mock 3 answer) gives 80, but both give +40; +80 comes from counting the 60m repayment as a supply, 340 - 260. Reasons, trap operators (b dropped-term -> sibling-swap) and trap explanation rewritten. Key C (280 - 320 = -40) unchanged.

It now reads 0.42017 + 0.43478 = 0.85495 > 0.85470 (= 1/1.17). Step 3 now gives the spot rates that backward induction through the printed tree produces (python3): 17.00%, 16.98%, 16.95%, 16.91% for 1-4 years, which confirms 'slightly downward sloping' and 'a few basis points'.
